name: Hemsedal

seo.title: Hemsedal ski resort guide
seo.description: 810 metres of vertical over three peaks, 22 lifts and 47 slopes, and 6 km of uninterrupted skiing from Totten at 1,450 metres.
seo.twitterDescription: 810 m of vertical, 22 lifts, 47 slopes and three peaks.
seo.webpageDescription: Ski facts, slopes by grade, where to stay and how to get to Hemsedal in Buskerud, Norway.

h1: Hemsedal ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Hemsedal has the largest vertical in this batch at 810 metres, spread over three peaks. From Totten at 1,450 metres you can ski six kilometres without stopping, 31 of the 47 slopes are graded very easy or easy, and the mountain takes 326 centimetres of snow a year.
stayOverview: Hemsedal splits between the ski centre at the lifts and the village down the valley. The first is for the first lift and the children's areas; the second is where the restaurants are.
hotelIntro: Book against high season and decide which end you want: the lift or the restaurants. The two are a bus ride apart.
rentalCars: A car helps for moving between the ski centre and the village, and Hemsedal is about three hours from Oslo by road.

travelTips.title: Two thirds is gentle

travelTips.sourceLabel: SkiStar: Hemsedal lifts, slopes and weather

travelTips.title: Six kilometres without stopping
travelTips.text: From Totten 2 at 1,450 metres you can ski six kilometres of uninterrupted slope.

travelTips.title: Off-piste next to the piste
travelTips.text: The resort puts its off-piste skiing right beside the groomed slopes rather than away from them.

highlights.title: Totten 2
highlights.text: The highest of the three peaks at 1,450 metres, with six kilometres of uninterrupted skiing from the top.

highlights.title: The beginner slopes
highlights.text: Twenty-one of the 47 slopes are graded very easy, more than any other resort in this batch.

highlights.title: The terrain park
highlights.text: A park and off-piste skiing laid out next to the groomed runs.

highlights.title: The cross-country network
